title: Tier Convention Table: The Window a Strip Notice Is Measured Over
content:
When a liability notice for test strips on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program is sized, the window over which strip refills are counted, the 30-day blocks it spans and what is measured against it follow the tier's refill length and its prior authorization requirement.

**Convention.** On a tier whose supply days per shipment are 30 and whose prior authorization is not required, the window is the one calendar month ending on the ship date, a strip refill falling in it when its ship date is later than the same calendar day one month earlier, that window spans one 30-day block, and what is measured against it is one third of the coverage. On a tier whose prior authorization is required, the window is that one calendar month, spanning one 30-day block, and what is measured against it is not the coverage but the units approved on the program's latest payer prior authorization for test strips, divided by the whole 30-day blocks of its approved span, never fewer than one block, and multiplied by the strips per billing unit, nothing being measured against the window when the program holds no payer prior authorization for test strips. On any other tier the window is the 3 calendar months ending on the ship date, spanning three 30-day blocks, and what is measured against it is the whole coverage.

| Tier | Supply days per shipment | Prior authorization required | Window | Blocks spanned | Measured against the window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Testing Supplies Self-Pay Program | 30 | No | 1 calendar month | 1 | one third of the coverage |
| Testing Supplies Commercial HMO Program | 30 | No | 1 calendar month | 1 | one third of the coverage |
| Testing Supplies Commercial PPO Program | 90 | No | 3 calendar months | 3 | the whole coverage |
| Testing Supplies Medicare Advantage Program | 90 | No | 3 calendar months | 3 | the whole coverage |
| Testing Supplies Original Medicare Program | 90 | No | 3 calendar months | 3 | the whole coverage |
| Testing Supplies Medicaid Program | 30 | Yes | 1 calendar month | 1 | the latest prior authorization's approved units per whole 30-day block of its span (at least one block), in strips; nothing without such an authorization |

- The *latest payer prior authorization for test strips* is the authorization grant for test strips with the basis payer prior authorization and the latest decision date. Its approved span runs from its valid-from date through its valid-through date, both days counted, and its whole 30-day blocks are those days divided by 30 and rounded down.
- A strip refill falls in a 3-month window when its ship date is later than the same calendar day 3 months earlier.

**Examples (hypothetical figures)**

- Coverage 240 strips on a 30-day tier without prior authorization: 80 strips are measured against a one-month window.
- A prior authorization approving 48 units for 1 January through 31 December: 365 days hold 12 whole blocks; 48 divided by 12 is 4 units, times 50, that is 200 strips measured against the one-month window.
- A prior authorization approving 2 units for a span of 20 days: the span holds no whole block, so it counts as one block, and 100 strips are measured.
- A prior-authorization tier on which the program holds no payer prior authorization for test strips: nothing is measured against the window.
